items.title: 3D reconstruction of a model phytophagous mite at nano-resolution reveals a peculiar ingestion and digestion system and structural adaptation for a tiny animal
items.title_zh: 3D reconstruction of a model phytophagous mite at nano-resolution reveals a peculiar ingestion and digestion system and structural adaptation for a tiny animal
items.summary: , has been elucidated using serial block-face scanning electron microscopy (SBF-SEM) combined with 3D reconstruction. The reconstructed models reveal previously unknown internal adaptations tailored to its unique lifestyle. These include a specialized food ingestion structure to facilitate effective cell-sucking, a semi-closed-loop tracheal system optimized for efficient oxygen diffusion in a minute organism, and a pair of well-developed silk glands utilized for water repellency, defense and dispersion. Notably, the midgut occupies nearly the entire body cavity, housing 189 (male) and 636 (female) suspended digestive cells, except for the reproductive system. No observable connections or channels were found linking two midgut regions (ventriculus and posterior midgut), nor were valve structures or controlling muscles detected in this region in most cases, suggesting the presence of an intermittent, dynamically regulated midgut. This adaptation may address the functional demands of unique digestive cells suspended within the ventriculus. However, a funnel-shaped midgut capable of forming temporary channels for the disabled transport of digestive cells from the ventriculus to the posterior midgut was identified. These findings profoundly advance our understanding of how minute animals adapt their internal systems to specialized lifestyles.

items.title: Accurate pathologic classification of aggressive myocarditis improves insights into patient precise medicine
items.title_zh: Accurate pathologic classification of aggressive myocarditis improves insights into patient precise medicine
items.summary: Because the disease's heterogeneity is ignored, the current diagnosis of myocarditis with advanced heart failure is imprecise, and there are no established criteria for subtyping this type of myocarditis. We analyzed data from 83 consecutive patients with aggressive myocarditis using a deep learning method to categorize them into three prognostically relevant phenogroups (PGs) based on myocardial whole-slide images: PG1, characterized by structural damage; PG2, dominated by autoimmune response; and PG3, driven by infections. Whole-exome sequencing of all patients revealed a significant concentration of mutations in myocardial structure-related genes in PG1, with the titin gene ( TTN) being the most frequently mutated. In contrast, mutations in immune-related genes were more prevalent in PG2 and PG3. RNA sequencing revealed unique molecular signatures: PG1 was associated with apoptosis, fibrosis, and the activation of abnormal metabolic pathways, whereas PG2 and PG3 were linked to cell damage and the activation of divergent immune pathways. Immunohistochemical staining suggested that PG1 and PG2 were characterized by T cell infiltration while PG3 was characterized by macrophage infiltration. In addition, the interleukin-6 signal transducer (IL6ST) was identified as a novel prognostic biomarker for myocarditis. A plasma IL6ST content ≥ 332.45 ng/ml was found to be associated with poor survival from recurrence symptom [hazard ratio (HR) 22.8, 95% confidence interval (CI) 2.3 to 227.2, Log-rank p value < 0.0001]. items.title: An aerogel-based light-driven knudsen pump approaching complete passive capturing of airborne particles in wide size ranges
items.title_zh: An aerogel-based light-driven knudsen pump approaching complete passive capturing of airborne particles in wide size ranges
items.summary: Aerosol sampling stands as an essential step in air quality monitoring and characterization. Active sampling provides accurate aerosol determination, while passive sampling offers cost-effective and power supply-free design. However, passive sampling is subject to sampling conditions and brings about uncertainties concerning particle sizes and flow rates, and collection efficiencies, which requires calibration assisted by active samplings. In this work, we presented a polyimide (PI) aerogel-based passive sampler operating in a flow-through and active-sampling mode without artificial power supply, generating a gas flow rate in the range of mL min -1 cm -2 (volume flow rate/surface area of PI aerogel) or cm min -1 , induced by light-driven thermal transpiration effects. It demonstrated a remarkably high collection efficiency of airborne particles approaching 100% in the particle range of 10 nm–10 µm, enabling the calibration-free sampling of airborne particles without requiring an additional power supply. We explored the effects of light intensity and pore size on the sampling performance, establishing a relationship between temperature gradient and flow rate. An analysis of the distribution and penetration of NaCl particles and real-world particles was conducted at the micrometer level, which exhibits a main penetration depth of < 100 µm. items.title: Analysis of critical conditions for air bubble detachment from freezing fronts under different gravitational environments
items.title_zh: Analysis of critical conditions for air bubble detachment from freezing fronts under different gravitational environments
items.summary: Extraterrestrial water resources like water ice are essential for space activities. Exploration of ice formation processes in different gravitational environments will contribute to developing and utilizing these water ice resources. The formation of air bubbles on freezing fronts during icing is a common phenomenon, and their behavior of detachment or trapping directly affects ice properties. Mathematical modeling of the forces acting on air bubbles on freezing fronts is developed to investigate air bubbles' detachment and trapping conditions under different gravitational accelerations. The main forces affecting the state of bubbles are the lift force composed of buoyant, Marangoni, and thermomolecular forces, and the drag force composed of adhesion force and gravity. The equilibrium of the lift force and drag force is the critical mechanical condition for air bubble detachment and trapping, and the bubble radius at this time is defined as the critical detachment radius. The experimentally validated mathematical model predicts the air bubble detachment radius with an accuracy of > 65%, which is higher than the 30% of the existing model. The analysis reveals that among the forces affecting the bubble state, the Marangoni and adhesion forces are the dominant factors. The tilt angle of the freezing front, temperature gradient, and liquid density affect the bubble detachment radius, with the temperature gradient having the greatest effect. items.title: Architecture and evolution of the lithosphere beneath the northern South China sea: Implications for plate-edge lithospheric thinning and rifting
items.title_zh: Architecture and evolution of the lithosphere beneath the northern South China sea: Implications for plate-edge lithospheric thinning and rifting
items.summary: Passive margins formed by continental rifting and oceanic spreading exhibit a wide range of characteristics, many of which remain poorly understood. In this study, we investigate the continent-ocean transition (COT) of the South China Sea (SCS) to elucidate the tectonic-magmatic processes involved in continental thinning and rifting. We present new in situ analyses of water, chemical, and Sr isotopic compositions of volcanic glasses and plagioclases, alongside the ages and Hf isotope compositions of zircons from the SCS. Our isotopic data reveal significant inter- and intra-crystalline disequilibria in plagioclase phenocrysts, suggesting a complex history of mantle-derived magmas interacting with the continental crust. Geochemical variability in the plagioclases and the presence of old inherited zircons indicate that mantle magmas were contaminated by crustal material. The ages (ranging from Cretaceous to Archean) and Hf isotopic signatures of the zircons are similar to those found in the Cathaysian block of Southeast China, supporting the presence of continental lithosphere beneath the northern SCS. The COT is characterized by a sharp juxtaposition of continental crust and igneous oceanic crust, and its structural features differ from the classic magma-poor or magma-rich passive-margin models. items.title: Association between chronic respiratory diseases and the attributable risk of long-term exposure to atmospheric particulate matters among middle-aged and elderly Chinese population
items.title_zh: Association between chronic respiratory diseases and the attributable risk of long-term exposure to atmospheric particulate matters among middle-aged and elderly Chinese population
items.summary: Chronic respiratory diseases (CRDs) mainly consist of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), asthma and chronic bronchitis. The attributable risks of CRDs associated with long-term exposure to ambient particulate matters (PMs, aerodynamic diameter ≤1, 2.5 and 10 µm: PM 1 , PM 2.5 and PM 10 ) are unclear, particularly in developing countries. We determined the association between long-term exposure to PMs and CRDs in the middle-aged and elderly Chinese population and their corresponding population-attributable fractions (PAF). We conducted a COPD Surveillance study in Guangdong, China. We derived the averaged 722-day exposure estimates of PM 1 , PM 2.5 and PM 10 at 1 km × 1 km resolution at individual residential addresses between 2013 and 2019. The associations between PMs and CRDs were estimated by logistic regression models. We calculated the PAF of CRDs attributable to long-term PM exposures. We included 7371 participants aged 40 years or greater, among whom 1430 (19.40%), 736 (9.99%), 731 (9.92%) and 313 (4.25%) had CRDs, COPD, chronic bronchitis and asthma, respectively. Each 10 µg/m 3 increment of PMs was positively associated with the proportion of patients with CRDs, COPD, chronic bronchitis and asthma. The associations were more prominent in participants residing in rural areas and exposed to biomass fuel. The PAF of CRDs associated with PM 1 , PM 2.5 and PM 10 was 19.09% (95%CI: 12.41%∼25.02%), 18.98% (95%CI: 12.90%∼24.90%) and 21.40% (95%CI: 13.84%∼27.67%), respectively. items.title: Brain-wide atlas of outputs and inputs of mouse auditory cortex revealed by modified viral labeling strategies
items.title_zh: Brain-wide atlas of outputs and inputs of mouse auditory cortex revealed by modified viral labeling strategies
items.summary: Understanding brain-wide connectivity is necessary to understand the principles of neural functions. While traditional neuron labeling methods have contributed to structural mapping, they often fall short in accurately identifying neuronal outputs because of limitations in solely using axon tracing. In this study, we improved labeling specificity by incorporating nuclear-localized fluorescent markers into retrograde and monosynaptic anterograde viral tracing strategies. Combined with high-resolution whole-brain imaging, this method enabled precise mapping of input-output relationships in the mouse auditory cortex (ACx). Soma-based labeling allowed for the clear identification of upstream and downstream neurons across the entire brain. Our analysis revealed that ACx projections to the primary somatosensory (SSp) and primary visual (VISp) cortices were largely restricted to layer 5, contrasting with previous reports suggesting stronger innervation in layers 1-3. We also identified downstream neurons within the corpus callosum (CC), a region not previously known to receive direct input from the ACx. These findings highlight the advantages of soma-targeted approaches in connectivity research and offer new insights into the organization of auditory networks. This approach lays the groundwork for future studies of circuit morphology and function across the brain.

items.title: Breaking hydrogen bond network enhances oxygenic photosynthesis of photosystem II
items.title_zh: Breaking hydrogen bond network enhances oxygenic photosynthesis of photosystem II
items.summary: Protein hydration water plays a crucial role in maintaining protein structures and functions, yet it remains challenging to manipulate. In this study, we use photosystem II (PS II), a protein complex consisting of 25 membrane proteins, as a model to explore the regulation of protein functions by modifying the hydration water structure. Within PS II, two water molecules are transported from the bulk solution through water channels into the oxygen-evolving center (OEC), where they are oxidized into oxygen. However, the role of water—both in hydrating PS II proteins and in transporting water through channels to the OEC—has often been overlooked. By studying the effects of different ions, including structure-making ions (Na + ) and breaking ions (K + ), on photosynthesis performance, we revealed distinctive different catalytic effects induced by these ions. Molecular dynamics simulations and Terahertz spectroscopy demonstrated that K + disrupts the hydrogen-bond network of hydration water, thereby facilitating water transportation to the O1 channel near the OEC, which in turn boosts oxygen evolution. In contrast, Na + did not exhibit the same effect. These findings underscore the essential role of K + in plant photosynthesis and reveal previously unrecognized mechanisms by which ions influence protein function through hydration water structure. The direct protein contacting water, termed hydration water, is closely linked to the kinetics and structures of proteins, thereby playing a crucial role in their functions. items.title: Comparative genomic analysis reveals spine formation and coral prostaglandin tolerance in crown-of-thorns starfish
items.title_zh: Comparative genomic analysis reveals spine formation and coral prostaglandin tolerance in crown-of-thorns starfish
items.summary: Recurring outbreaks of crown-of-thorns starfish (COTS) are one of the greatest threats to corals and have caused catastrophic damage to coral reef ecosystems in recent decades. As obligate corallivores, COTS can tolerate toxic coral mucus, and the sharp spines covering their bodies provide protection from predators. While both of these characteristics are known to contribute to the vitality of COTS and aggravate the impact of COTS outbreaks, the genetic mechanisms underlying their adaptation remain unclear. In this study, we generated a chromosome-level COTS genome and suggested the importance of chromosome fusion in coral-feeding adaptation. In addition, high expression levels of EP4 receptors in the COTS spine apex indicated their potential ability to use the coral prostaglandin PGE2, which might further activate the skeletogenic gene regulatory network responsible for the growth of the spine and body plan of COTS. A comparison of the historical population sizes of COTS from different locations revealed a unique trend in the Coral Triangle, suggesting a potentially higher risk of outbreaks in this region. Our results provide a molecular basis for the adaptive evolution of COTS and a better understanding of its interactions in coral reef ecosystems.

items.title_zh: Comparison of the biological effects of various radiation therapies for keloids by single-cell RNA sequencing reveals IRF1 as a novel target in keloid therapy
items.summary: Keloids are benign dermal tumors that arise from abnormal wound healing processes following skin lesions. Keloids are present in all human populations but occur most frequently in Africans. A significantly higher incidence is observed in female populations. Consequently, keloid patients not only endure physical burdens caused by symptoms such as pain, pruritus, and burning, but also suffer from psychological distress due to altered appearance, significantly compromising their quality of life. Surgical excision, as one of the various treatment options, demonstrates rapid efficacy but carries an unacceptably high recurrence rate of 40-100% when used as a standalone therapy. Postoperative radiotherapy (PORT) is a clinically effective measure to reduce recurrence rates of keloid. items.title_zh: Crystallographically aligned Wadsley-Roth phase anodes with conductive agents for high-rate lithium-ion batteries
items.summary: To realize high-energy density lithium-ion batteries, achieving fast-charging capabilities for electrodes with high areal mass loadings is a significant challenge. Traditional anode materials such as graphite and lithium titanate face limitations in fast charging owing to safety risks and energy density constraints. Wadsley-Roth structured niobium-based oxides have attracted attention for their unique three-dimensional open tunnel structures, but their low electrical conductivity limits practical applications. This study innovatively proposes a two-phase structural design with crystallographic alignment, successfully preparing a niobium titanium oxide (TiNb 2 O 7 )-conductive agent titanium oxide (Ti 4 O 7 ) anode material (TNO CA). By precisely controlling the sintering temperature, TNO CA achieves a crystallographic alignment between TNO and Ti 4 O 7 , significantly enhancing the electronic conductivity and ion transport properties of the material. items.title: ENSO-induced precipitation seasonality in the Chinese loess plateau during 1767–2050 CE
items.title_zh: ENSO-induced precipitation seasonality in the Chinese loess plateau during 1767–2050 CE
items.summary: Climate change has not only altered the total amount of rainfall but also significantly impacted its seasonal distribution. This alteration is particularly critical in monsoonal regions, where the availability and timing of water resources are essential for agricultural activities and ecological sustainability. However, the understanding of precipitation seasonality was largely constrained by the limitations of observational data. In this study, we present a reconstruction of seasonal precipitation patterns derived from the magnetic properties of a stalagmite collected from the Chinese Loess Plateau, which serves as a proxy for precipitation seasonality from 1767 to CE 2006. Our results indicate that magnetic-based precipitation seasonality exhibits significant fluctuations characterized by quasiperiodic oscillations with periodicities of 2-7 and 14 years. items.title: Effects of early-life tactile experience enrichment on autistic-like behaviors and synaptic alterations in Shank3 mutant mice
items.title_zh: Effects of early-life tactile experience enrichment on autistic-like behaviors and synaptic alterations in Shank3 mutant mice
items.summary: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) presents a significant therapeutic challenge due to limited treatment options. While non-pharmacological approaches based on sensory stimulation have shown promise in clinical practice, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study explored the therapeutic potential of tactile experience enrichment (TEE) during specific developmental windows in Shank3 KO mice, a model of ASD. We found that pre-weaning TEE robustly rescued core behavioral deficits, including social interaction and repetitive grooming, whereas juvenile TEE only improved social behavior. RNA sequencing of the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) and dorsolateral striatum (DLS) revealed TEE-induced alterations in synaptic gene expression, including the upregulation of the Polo-like kinase 1 (PLK-1) pathway, which may modulate synaptic maturation. Furthermore, pre-weaning TEE restored dendritic spine density and morphology, along with synaptic transmission, in both the ACC and DLS. These findings indicate that early tactile enrichment, particularly during the pre-weaning period, can effectively alleviate core ASD-related behaviors in Shank3 KO mice by modulating synaptic structure and function, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic intervention for ASD.

items.title: Evaluating plasticity of rejuvenated metallic glasses by effective enthalpy
items.title_zh: Evaluating plasticity of rejuvenated metallic glasses by effective enthalpy
items.summary: Structural rejuvenation is a promising strategy to enhance the plasticity of metallic glasses, but quantitatively evaluating the rejuvenation-deformation relationship is challenging. In this work, we systematically investigate the compressive plasticity of a typical Zr-based metallic glass which is rejuvenated by elastostatic compression or cycled twists. Meanwhile, the thermodynamics and structural properties are carefully characterized for these rejuvenated glasses. An obvious gap in the plastic strain ε p is observed between two sets of the rejuvenated glasses, although they have very close exothermic enthalpy ∆ H exo before glass transition. This plasticity gap is also reflected by the different modes of shear banding: straight for the elastostatic compression but deflected for the cycled twists. We use the concept of effective enthalpy Δ H eff and find a linear relationship between Δ H eff and ε p for all rejuvenated glasses. This implies that the plastic deformability of glasses is determined not only by the existing free volume evaluated by ∆ H exo but also by the creating free volume required to enter the supercooled liquid state, as evaluated by the endothermic glass transition overshoot. Synchrotron high-energy X-ray diffraction reveals that the larger ε p in glasses with higher Δ H eff arises from the enhanced structural heterogeneity caused by the decoupling of medium-range orders.

items.title: From searching for extraterrestrial biosignatures to exploring the origins of life: A prebiotic chemistry perspective
items.title_zh: From searching for extraterrestrial biosignatures to exploring the origins of life: A prebiotic chemistry perspective
items.summary: The search for extraterrestrial life represents one of humanity’s most profound scientific endeavors. This review examines the role of prebiotic chemistry in our quest to detect extraterrestrial life. Analyzing diverse chemical pathways, including the Strecker synthesis, cyanide polymerization, and Fischer-Tropsch-type reactions, outlines how simple inorganic precursors may evolve into complex chemical reaction networks under non-biological conditions. While compounds such as amino acids are common in both abiotic and biotic contexts, discerning their origins requires an understanding of reaction mechanisms, environmental contexts, and the thermodynamic challenges of polymerization. Moreover, this review addresses the emergence of homochirality and the development of genetic systems, proposing that these phenomena may arise from dynamic prebiotic processes. Laboratory simulations of extraterrestrial environments are crucial in testing these hypotheses, providing insights into the potential trajectories from simple monomers to complex macromolecules under planetary surface and interstellar conditions. Ultimately, this review advocates for reassessing biosignature interpretation methods, underscoring the need for integrated, multifaceted approaches that consider both prebiotic chemical evolution and environmental context when evaluating the potential for life beyond Earth. items.title: H4K20me3 erasure facilitates reprogramming to totipotent-like state by promoting DUX4 mediated transcription
items.title_zh: H4K20me3 erasure facilitates reprogramming to totipotent-like state by promoting DUX4 mediated transcription
items.summary: Epigenetic remodeling following fertilization is essential for the acquisition of embryonic totipotency. The role of H4K20me3, a key epigenetic modification, remains largely unexplored in the context of early human embryogenesis. Here, we observed a dynamic erasure of H4K20me3 modification during zygotic genome activation (ZGA), followed by a re-establishment after ZGA in human embryos. Using in vitro reprogramming to totipotent-like states, we demonstrated that transient removal of H4K20me3 in human embryonic stem cells promotes DUX4 -mediated expression of totipotent genes and facilitates the transition into a totipotent-like state. Mechanistically, we show that H4K20me3 preferentially accumulates around genes specific to the 8-cell-like state, which are induced by DUX4 and repressed by H4K20me3 modification. Furthermore, H4K20me3 enrichment near pericentromeric regions may regulate satellite repeat transcripts, which have been shown to participate in heterochromatin remodeling and totipotency reprogramming. Our findings suggest that active erasure of H4K20me3 at the human ZGA stage plays a role in facilitating the expression of totipotency genes, thereby reinforcing early human embryo development.

items.title: Healthy lifestyle attenuates the clonal hematopoiesis-associated coronary artery disease risk
items.title_zh: Healthy lifestyle attenuates the clonal hematopoiesis-associated coronary artery disease risk
items.summary: Lifestyle factors and clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) both contribute to the risk of developing coronary artery disease (CAD), but whether a healthy lifestyle could attenuate CHIP-related CAD risk is unknown. A total of 6113 participants from the Prediction for Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease Risk in China project were included. Lifestyle was categorized as unfavorable, intermediate, and favorable according to the number of healthy lifestyle factors (body mass index, smoking, sleep, physical activity, and diet). CHIP mutations were detected by targeted deep sequencing (mean depth, 916 ×). After a median follow-up of 12.1 years, 760 cases of CAD were recorded. A favorable lifestyle and CHIP were associated with 53% lower (HR (hazard ratio) = 0.47; 95% CI (confidence interval): 0.36-0.61) and 41% higher (HR = 1.41; 95% CI: 1.17-1.72) CAD risk, respectively. Of note, the elevated CAD risk attributed to CHIP was found in the intermediate (HR = 1.48; 95% CI: 1.03-2.11) and unfavorable (HR = 1.57; 95% CI: 1.22-2.01) lifestyle groups, but not in the favorable (HR = 0.71; 95% CI: 0.36-1.42) group. items.title: High-performance seismic response analysis for mega-scale integrated underground-aboveground structure system in saturated sand
items.title_zh: High-performance seismic response analysis for mega-scale integrated underground-aboveground structure system in saturated sand
items.summary: With rapid urbanization, major cities are witnessing mass development of large integrated underground-aboveground structure systems. A notable example is the Beijing Municipal Administrative Center Transport Complex (BMACTC), which boasts an underground area spanning 1.28 million square meters. The soil-structure interaction and mutual interaction among structure components, particularly in liquefiable sites, pose significant challenges for seismic design. To address these challenges, this study proposes a high-performance solid-fluid coupled elastoplastic simulation method for earthquake geotechnical engineering, and applies it to achieve integrated simulation of BMACTC with a finite element method (FEM) model of over 16 million degrees of freedom. The analysis unveils the seismic response of underground structures under the influence of large openings, aboveground structures, and cross-section changes. Saturated sand layers experience significant weakening under seismic loading, with a maximum excess pore pressure ratio of nearly 0.5. The large openings significantly increase the nearby horizontal deformation and uplift of the underground structure. Moderate height and tall aboveground structures have different effects on the deformation of the underground structure, which is related to the system natural frequency and input motion frequency. The change in cross section geometry affects the deformation and internal force in the transition zone between the different sections.

items.title: Highly selective electrochemical synthesis of ClO 2 from chlorite with Ti 4 O 7 for rapid pollutants degradation and safe disinfection
items.title_zh: Highly selective electrochemical synthesis of ClO 2 from chlorite with Ti 4 O 7 for rapid pollutants degradation and safe disinfection
items.summary: Industrial synthesis of chlorine dioxide (ClO 2 ) is infrastructure-demanding and presents significant safety and transportation challenges. The electrochemical method, while offering an on-site ClO 2 production alternative, suffers from risky chlorate (ClO 3 − ) generation, even when using a widely-utilized noble metal-based dimensionally stable anode (DSA). In this study, we report that a Ti 4 O 7 anode can efficiently convert chlorite (ClO 2 − , 25 mmol L −1 ) to ClO 2 with an impressive selectivity of 99% at 10 mA cm −2 . Unlike DSA, which generates abundant free hydroxyl radicals (•OH) that over-oxidize ClO 2 − into ClO 3 − via a 2:1 stoichiometry, the Ti 4 O 7 anode confines •OH onto its surface, facilitating selective ClO 2 − oxidation through single-electron transfer reaction. With this novel Ti 4 O 7 anode, a portable ClO 2 gas generator was designed to continuously deliver high-purity and cost-effective ClO 2 at a rate of 3.30 g h −1 with high stability over 5-day operational period, and thus is very promising for rapid water pollutants (sulfamethazine, ciprofloxacin, cephalexin, tetracycline, and carbamazepine) degradation and safe disinfection against pathogens ( E. coli, S. aureus , and AR E. coli ) in minutes with minimal chlorinated byproducts.
items.title_en: Highly selective electrochemical synthesis of ClO 2 from chlorite with Ti 4 O 7 for rapid pollutants degradation and safe disinfection

items.title: How a healthy lifestyle mediates socioeconomic inequities in healthy ageing and life expectancies: A 20-year cohort of older adults
items.title_zh: How a healthy lifestyle mediates socioeconomic inequities in healthy ageing and life expectancies: A 20-year cohort of older adults
items.summary: Lower socioeconomic status (SES) is associated with various adverse health outcomes, but its association with healthy ageing is less known, and whether adherence to a healthy lifestyle at late-life years can reduce socioeconomic disparities in health requires further investigation. In a 20-year cohort of 33,541 older adults aged ≥65 years across 23 provinces in China, we investigated socioeconomic disparities in mortality and unhealthy ageing considering physical, cognitive, mental, visual, and hearing functions, and evaluated whether adherence to a healthy lifestyle at late-life years can reduce these health disparities. We categorized SES into low, medium, or high using latent class analysis based on education level, financial status, and occupation, and established the healthy lifestyle score by never smoking, no heavy alcohol consumption, regular physical and leisure activity, and a healthy diet. Compared with older adults of high SES, those of low SES had increased risks of all-cause mortality and unhealthy ageing, with adjusted hazard ratios (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) of 1.25 (1.17, 1.33) and 1.46 (1.33, 1.60), respectively. Overall, a healthy lifestyle mediated 20.5% (16.4, 24.7) and 16.4% (12.0, 20.9) of socioeconomic inequity in all-cause mortality and unhealthy ageing, respectively. items.title: Interfacial spin configurations and the microscopic origin of exchange bias at the IrMn/CoFeB interface
items.title_zh: Interfacial spin configurations and the microscopic origin of exchange bias at the IrMn/CoFeB interface
items.summary: Exchange bias fields at antiferromagnet/ferromagnet (AFM/FM) interfaces play a crucial role in the performance of spintronic devices. Despite extensive research, the physical origin of exchange bias remains incompletely understood. In this study, we conduct a detailed investigation of a prototype AFM/FM interface widely used in spintronic applications, i.e., the IrMn/CoFeB interface. High-resolution synchrotron X-ray measurements reveal the existence of uncompensated Mn spins at the interface. While most of these spins are strongly coupled to the adjacent CoFeB layer, a small fraction remains pinned to the underlying IrMn underlayer. Element-specific X-ray magnetic circular dichroism hysteresis loops show that these pinned spins can be switched by increasing the annealing magnetic field. Furthermore, micromagnetic simulations indicate that an imbalance in the quantity of antiparallel pinned spins contributes to the observed variation in exchange bias. Overall, these findings offer important insights into the microscopic mechanisms governing exchange bias and its tunability.
items.title_en: Interfacial spin configurations and the microscopic origin of exchange bias at the IrMn/CoFeB interface

items.title: Intraoperative temporal interference (TI)-noninvasive brain stimulation prevents postoperative delirium in mice
items.title_zh: Intraoperative temporal interference (TI)-noninvasive brain stimulation prevents postoperative delirium in mice
items.summary: Postoperative delirium (POD), a common neurocognitive complication in the early postoperative period associated with high morbidity in elderly and high-risk surgical patients, faces fundamental research constraints due to the lack of quantitative rodent behavioral assessment tools, hindering therapeutic innovation. Herein, we employed a 3D-AI animal behavior analysis system to evaluate spontaneous behaviors in mice post laparotomy surgery with isoflurane anesthesia. Mice exhibited apathy, bradykinesia, inflexible motion, and abnormal behavioral transitions at the 3-day after surgery. Based on unsupervised clustering and manifold analysis, we then quantized the dynamic alteration of comprehensive behavioral phenotypes in fear conditioning test. The cued memory, cognitive flexibility, and cognitive robustness were also impaired after surgery. Furthermore, we developed a novel intraoperative temporal interference-noninvasive brain stimulation (TI-NIBS), inducing a stereo-focusing electric field targeting the dentate gyrus of dorsal hippocampus, which significantly mitigated POD symptoms by restoring hippocampal neural activity and neurotransmitter homeostasis. This study elucidates a comprehensive behavioral profile of POD symptoms and provides a therapeutic non-invasive neuro-modulatory strategy to prevent POD by restoring hippocampal function.
items.title_en: Intraoperative temporal interference (TI)-noninvasive brain stimulation prevents postoperative delirium in mice

items.title: Large-scale evidence for highly coupled soil multi-elements in permafrost ecosystems
items.title_zh: Large-scale evidence for highly coupled soil multi-elements in permafrost ecosystems
items.summary: The coupled soil element cycles are the foundation of many crucial ecosystem functions such as primary production and climate regulation. However, whether and how multiple soil elements are coupled in permafrost regions remains unclear. Here, we collected and analyzed 240 soil samples from the active layer (0-10 cm) and permafrost deposits (top 50 cm) at 24 sites along a 1000-km transect on the Tibetan Plateau. We found that a high degree of soil element coupling, defined as the mean Spearman rank correlation among 19 measured elements, was maintained in the two soil layers. Nutrient elements were more likely to be coupled than non-nutrient elements, with 19 and 11 sites revealing robust coupling of nutrient and non-nutrient elements, respectively. Furthermore, atomic properties, including atomic mass and electronegativity, affected element coupling in the active layer, but had no effect in the permafrost deposits. These findings advance our understanding of terrestrial biogeochemistry in permafrost regions and inspire further research to explore the linkage of soil element coupling with ecosystem functioning.
items.title_en: Large-scale evidence for highly coupled soil multi-elements in permafrost ecosystems

items.title: Magnetic catheter robot with dynamic force feedback for stiffness identification and abnormality detection
items.title_zh: Magnetic catheter robot with dynamic force feedback for stiffness identification and abnormality detection
items.summary: Magnetic continuum robots offer unique advantages for minimally invasive surgery owing to their flexibility, miniaturization, and remote actuation. However, the absence of reliable real-time force feedback in existing magnetically actuated catheters severely constrains safe interaction, and quantitative identification of tissue mechanical properties. To address this limitation, this work presents a magnetic catheter robot with integrated dynamic force feedback. The proposed system integrates an axial optical force sensor, a miniaturized endoscope, and annular permanent magnets within a compact distal architecture. This design achieves sub-0.01 N force resolution while remaining robust under large bending deformations and varying deflection angles. System performance is quantitatively evaluated through force-controlled planar writing, 3D curved-surface palpation with shape perception and stiffness mapping, and endoscope-guided bronchial palpation, demonstrating reliable stiffness-based abnormality detection in complex luminal environments. These results demonstrate the feasibility of force-aware magnetic catheterization for quantitative assessment of local tissue mechanics, providing a clinically relevant platform for minimally invasive diagnostics.

items.title: Mechanism-directed design and synthesis of a dinuclear copper porphyrin for efficient electrocatalytic hydrogen evolution reaction
items.title_zh: Mechanism-directed design and synthesis of a dinuclear copper porphyrin for efficient electrocatalytic hydrogen evolution reaction
items.summary: Developing efficient catalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is vital for a H 2 -based energy system. Designing catalysts based on the HER mechanisms is required but has been rarely achieved. Herein, we report on a dinuclear Cu porphyrin for HER. We recently identified an intermolecular electron transfer mechanism in the HER with Cu porphyrins. We consider realizing intramolecular electron transfer between Cu porphyrins to improve HER. By linking two porphyrin units through an alkynyl group, we synthesized dinuclear Cu porphyrin 1 with two conjugated porphyrin units. Electrochemical studies confirm the effective interaction between the two Cu porphyrin units. Importantly, for HER electrocatalysis, the i cat / i p value with 1 (204) is seven times larger than that with its mononuclear analogue (29). Experimental and theoretical studies confirm intramolecular electron transfer in the HER with 1 . This work is therefore significant in presenting a mechanism-directed design of 1 as a highly active HER catalyst.
items.title_en: Mechanism-directed design and synthesis of a dinuclear copper porphyrin for efficient electrocatalytic hydrogen evolution reaction

items.title: Modulation of nociceptive nerve activity as a novel therapeutic strategy in acute myeloid leukemia
items.title_zh: Modulation of nociceptive nerve activity as a novel therapeutic strategy in acute myeloid leukemia
items.summary: Emerging evidence has highlighted a critical role of the neuro-microenvironment in regulating hematopoiesis and hematologic malignancies. However, how malignant cells remodel the neural compartment and how these neural changes in turn influence disease progression remain poorly understood. In this study, we mapped the spatial distribution of sympathetic (TH + ) and nociceptive (CGRP + ) nerve fibers in the bone marrow and spleen under steady-state conditions and during acute myeloid leukemia (AML) using immunofluorescence imaging. We found that AML induces a reduction of nerve fiber density at the early stage of AML and that leukemic cells preferentially accumulate in neural-sparse regions. Functional investigations revealed that pharmacological ablation of nociceptive nerves via capsaicin accelerated leukemic progression and disrupted stressed hematopoiesis. Conversely, activation of nociceptive nerves by dietary capsaicin delayed AML onset and improved overall survival. Further mechanistic investigation revealed that the CGRP–RAMP1 axis inhibits leukemia progression by suppressing the TNF-α pathway in AML cells. These findings highlight the anti-leukemic role of nociceptive nerves and suggest therapeutic potential for neural modulation in AML.

items.title: Optical demodulation and multi-dimensional identification via a monolithic perovskite heterojunction
items.title_zh: Optical demodulation and multi-dimensional identification via a monolithic perovskite heterojunction
items.summary: Position sensitive detectors (PSDs) based on the lateral photovoltaic effect (LPE) are distinguished by their non-contact sensing capabilities and exceptional self-powered properties, showcasing significant potential for diverse applications. However, the development of high-performance detectors that meet the demands of intelligent perception, particularly those capable of acquiring complex information from optical fields, remains a significant challenge. In this work, we propose a PSD utilizing an ITO/MAPbI 3 :P(VDF-TrFE)/Si heterojunction, which successfully achieves a broadband self-powered response ranging from 405 to 1064 nm. The modulation of the pyroelectric field enables a position sensitivity (PS) of 688.10 mV/mm, representing a substantial enhancement of 144.13%. Simultaneously, the pyroelectric effect is found to significantly enhance the wavelength resolution. The device effectively decodes the digital information encoded with position-related ASCII code by directly evaluating the lateral photovoltage (LPV) values of the PSD across the visible to near-infrared spectrum, facilitating position and wavelength-resolved photoelectric demodulation. Furthermore, the PSD can mutually distinguish the wavelength, position, and intensity of incident light based on the LPV values and their enhancement ratios, without the need for additional systems, thus enabling the identification and coding of multi-dimensional optical information.

items.title: Passive decoy state quantum secure direct communication
items.title_zh: Passive decoy state quantum secure direct communication
items.summary: The decoy state method is an effective approach for addressing the source imperfections in quantum communication. By employing pulses of varying intensities to estimate error rates and yields, this method requires active modulation of the source intensity. However, the active modulation operation may introduce side-channel vulnerabilities, potentially allowing an eavesdropper to execute Trojan horse attacks. The passive decoy state method circumvents this issue by eliminating the need for active intensity modulation. In this paper, we propose a passive decoy state quantum secure direct communication (QSDC) protocol that generates weak coherent states with random intensities using two phase-randomized coherent pulses. Leveraging linear optics, our protocol facilitates straightforward implementation and is robust against eavesdropping side-channel attacks targeting source intensity modulators.We establish a system model for the protocol and derive its secrecy message capacity. Additionally, we optimize the input intensities of the protocol and obtain the maximum secrecy message capacity for each channel attenuation value. Compared with the previous protocol, our protocol exhibits an approximately 25% enhancement in the secrecy message transmission rate within a channel attenuation range of 6 dB. We also compare the performance of the three-decoy-state protocol with that of the infinite-decoy-state protocol. items.title_zh: Pure oxygen terminated MXenes prepared by NaOH/NaI eutectic molten salt
items.summary: MXenes, a promising class of two-dimensional materials derived from transition metal carbides and nitrides, are attracting considerable attention for their remarkable properties and potential uses in energy storage, EMI shielding, electronics, etc. Modifying surface terminations is essential for tuning the electron structure of MXenes, significantly affecting their properties. However, existing methods for altering the surface chemistry, particularly regarding oxygen termination, encounter significant challenges, such as low substitution efficiency and self-oxidation during treatment, resulting in the absence of pure O-terminated MXenes in the literature. items.title: Radiotherapy followed by metformin neoadjuvant therapy drives superior pancreatic cancer ferroptosis and augments anti-tumor immunity
items.title_zh: Radiotherapy followed by metformin neoadjuvant therapy drives superior pancreatic cancer ferroptosis and augments anti-tumor immunity
items.summary: Although neoadjuvant therapy has achieved higher levels of resectability and improved the survival outcomes of pancreatic carcinoma patients, cancer cells' resistance to conventional cell death has limited its clinical efficiency. Thus, developing an optimal sequence of novel neoadjuvant therapy modalities to boost cancer cell death is urgently needed. The current work addresses this issue by developing a combination of radiotherapy with metformin as a novel neoadjuvant therapy and investigating its optimal sequencing treatment to boost cancer cell ferroptosis. Of the three treatment regimens investigated, the sequential treatment with RT followed by metformin (i.e. as opposed to metformin followed by RT, or simultaneous treatment with both RT and metformin) was most effective in eliciting ferroptosis in vitro and in animal models. Mechanically, RT followed by metformin is dependent on the inhibition of the AMPK-GOT1 axis, which further leads to the arrest of cancer cells in G1/S phase, and ultimately ferroptosis. Moreover, using a combination of patient samples and mouse models, RT followed by metformin enhanced the anti-tumor immune cells (IFNγ + CD8 + T cells, DC cells, and M1 macrophage) infiltration and cytokines (IFN-γ and IL-2) level, inhibited the pro-tumor immune cells (PD-1 + TIM3 + CD8 + T cells and M2 macrophage) infiltration and cytokines (TGF-β and IL-10) level. Overall, the study developed an optimal sequencing of neoadjuvant therapy modality that induced superior cancer cell ferroptosis and boosted anti-tumor immunity, which presented a promising therapeuti…

items.title: Recent advances in customizing the electrostatic potential pore environments of metal-organic frameworks for C 2 H 2 and C 2 H 4 purification
items.title_zh: Recent advances in customizing the electrostatic potential pore environments of metal-organic frameworks for C 2 H 2 and C 2 H 4 purification
items.summary: High-purity acetylene (C 2 H 2 ) and ethylene (C 2 H 4 ) are valuable and critical chemicals, whereas the impurities with closely similar structures and properties pose significant challenges for their purifications. Inspired by biological recognition systems, adsorptive separation based on the discrimination of electrostatic potential (ESP) differences among gas molecules has emerged as a promising approach for gas-mixture separation. Compared to traditional kinetic and thermodynamic mechanisms, ESP-driven separations demonstrate advantages such as high separation selectivity, fast diffusion rate, and facile regeneration. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advancements in the rational design of metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) with tailored ESP pore environments, highlighting their applications in ESP-driven separation processes for producing high-purity C 2 H 2 and C 2 H 4 . Furthermore, we summarize and discuss the strategies for modifying MOF adsorbents and the characterization techniques employed to elucidate their underlying separation mechanisms. Lastly, this review outlines current challenges and future prospects in this field, aiming to provide valuable insights into ongoing research for achieving efficient ESP-driven separation for complex gas-mixtures in a single step.

items.title: Recent advances in integrated biophysical and biochemical microfluidic methods for circulating tumor cells isolation and analysis
items.title_zh: Recent advances in integrated biophysical and biochemical microfluidic methods for circulating tumor cells isolation and analysis
items.summary: Cancer is a worldwide public health problem. Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) are one of the most significant tumor biomarkers, reflecting critical information of disease transcriptome, genome, and proteome. Various microfluidic methods have been proposed to separate, detect and analyze CTCs, involving multiple processes. In this work, we aim to give a comprehensive overview on recent advances in integrated biophysical and biochemical microfluidic methods for CTCs separation and detection. First, early label-free biophysical methods are introduced and discussed, including basic passive and active approaches as well as active-passive integrated assays. Next, we summarize labelled methods with different biochemical reactions based on their unique working principles, such as immune affinity-based methods and magnetic nanoparticle-assisted methods. Moreover, the most dominating approaches combining biochemical and biophysical methods are discussed. Their applicability and unique features are compared. Finally, we offer the perspectives on integrated microfluidic approaches for CTCs biosensing and cancer diagnostics.

items.title: Speeding up adiabatic holonomic quantum gates via π -pulse modulation
items.title_zh: Speeding up adiabatic holonomic quantum gates via π -pulse modulation
items.summary: Holonomic quantum computation (HQC) offers an inherently robust approach to quantum gate implementation by exploiting quantum holonomies. While adiabatic HQC benefits from robustness against certain control errors, its long runtime limits practical utility due to increased exposure to environmental noise. Nonadiabatic HQC addresses this issue by enabling faster gate operations but compromises robustness. In this work, we propose a scheme for fast holonomic quantum gates based on the π -pulse method, which accelerates adiabatic evolution while preserving its robustness. By guiding the system Hamiltonian along geodesic paths in the parameter space and applying phase-modulating π pulses at discrete points, we realize a universal set of holonomic gates beyond the conventional adiabatic limit. Our scheme allows for arbitrary single-qubit and two-qubit controlled gates within a single-loop evolution and provides additional tunable parameters for flexible gate design. These results demonstrate a promising path toward high-fidelity, fast, and robust quantum computation .

items.title: Stimulating the non-ARG harbored microbes with a specific carbon source can suppress the rebound of soil ARB after calcium peroxide application
items.title_zh: Stimulating the non-ARG harbored microbes with a specific carbon source can suppress the rebound of soil ARB after calcium peroxide application
items.summary: The spread of antibiotic resistance genes poses a significant global environmental risk. Soil antibiotic-resistant bacteria (ARB) are a critical reservoir for antibiotic resistance genes in the environment, making them a focal point of concern. Traditional abatement techniques are not suitable for field applications at present. In this study, we investigated the removal of soil ARB using a combination of calcium peroxide and D-mannitol. Treatment with 2% CaO 2 alone effectively reduced the populations of sulfonamide-resistant bacteria, beta-lactam-resistant bacteria, macrolide-resistant bacteria, and tetracycline-resistant bacteria by over 90% under a soil water holding capacity of 90%. However, this reduction decreased significantly after 40 days due to CaO 2 depletion. To sustain the removal effect, we screened carbon sources and found that adding 1 mM D-mannitol 10 days after applying CaO 2 could maintain removal rates of 78.41%, 91.44%, 86.81%, and 90.39% after 40 days. Sequencing results revealed that while CaO 2 alone initially reduced ARB, it led to a rebound in genera such as Ochrobactrum and Lysinibacillus . In contrast, D-mannitol addition prevented this rebound and enriched non-ARB genera like Nitrososphaera , enhancing the overall removal effect. This study demonstrates that combining CaO 2 with D-mannitol is a promising strategy for efficient and sustained removal of soil ARB.

items.summary: Treatment with combined immune checkpoint blockade (CICB) has been considered as an effective approach to increase the objective response rate for cancer immunotherapy, but at the cost of significantly increased immune-related adverse events (irAEs) and also sufferings from drug resistance due to the transitory working manner of antibody-based ICB inhibitors. items.title: Targeting C3aR/STAT3 signaling attenuates neuroinflammation and reverses neurological impairment in Neuromyelitis optica
items.title_zh: Targeting C3aR/STAT3 signaling attenuates neuroinflammation and reverses neurological impairment in Neuromyelitis optica
items.summary: Abundant evidence indicates that the interaction between astrocytes and microglia through the C3-C3a receptor (C3aR) pathway is a crucial contributor to the pathogenesis of neurodegenerative and autoimmune disorders, such as neuromyelitis optica (NMO). However, the role of C3aR in microglia in modulating inflammation related to local lesions and neurological dysfunctions in NMO remains unclear. In this study, we reveal for the first time that the expression of C3aR on microglia is positively correlated with microglial activation, proinflammatory cytokine secretion, and complement deposition, which results in the typical NMO-like lesion characterized by astrocyte injury with aquaporin 4 (AQP4) loss, demyelination, and motor neuron loss, as well as cognitive impairments, visual defects, and locomotor deficits in different models of NMO. The knockdown of C3aR or the use of a C3aR antagonist, both ex vivo and in vivo , effectively attenuates neuroinflammation, alleviates pathological lesions, and rescues neurological functions. Mechanistically, we identify STAT3 as a downstream target of microglial C3aR signalling that functionally mediates NMO pathogenesis. Blocking the C3aR/STAT3 cascade restores motor and visual functions by reducing the release of proinflammatory factors. Taken together, our study demonstrates a key role of the C3aR-STAT3 pathway in regulating neuroinflammation in NMO pathology and provides potential targets for therapeutic intervention.

items.title: The dividend period of climate change–related mortality in China is coming to an end
items.title_zh: The dividend period of climate change–related mortality in China is coming to an end
items.summary: Health risks posed by temperature have aroused concern among scientists and the public. Previous studies have consistently projected a downward trend in the cold-related health burden and an upward trend in the heat-related burden under climate change. However, the temporal trend of the net effect of temperature and the existence of a descent phase for adaptation remain unclear. Here, we propose a new concept, the dividend period of climate change-related mortality, defined as the period when the net health effect of temperature exhibits a downward trend. We project a region-specific dividend period in China under climate change and adaptability scenarios. The results indicate that human adaptability substantially influences the temperature-mortality association and that the dividend period varies markedly by region and urbanization. After considering adaptability and population changes, the dividend period in the central and western regions has either ended or is coming to an end under most scenarios and will end before the 2050s in the northeastern region. In contrast, the dividend period in the eastern region will extend to the end of the 21st century but will soon end under certain scenarios. Our findings highlight the urgent need for more effective climate change mitigation and adaptation actions, particularly in regions at the end of the dividend period in the near future.

items.title: Transcranial direct current stimulation and lesions hierarchically reorganize brain network dynamics with biological annotations
items.title_zh: Transcranial direct current stimulation and lesions hierarchically reorganize brain network dynamics with biological annotations
items.summary: Mapping human brain function based on neuromodulation and lesions could reorganize brain network dynamics and uncover causal relationships with behaviors or symptoms. However, the principles of reorganization, neural mechanisms, and clinical implications underlying brain network dynamics in response to such modulations remain unclear. Here, we leveraged large-scale fMRI data and perturbation approaches to modulate brain network dynamics, investigating their associations with multi-level micro-architectural profiles including neurotransmitter receptors and transporters, cell types, laminar differentiation, microstructure, cortical expansion, and metabolism. We found that neuromodulation and lesions modulating the prefrontal and motor cortices led to distinct and opposing reorganizations in the topographic distribution of network dynamics along the sensorimotor-association hierarchy. Moreover, we observed a predominant co-localization between the reorganizations and micro-architectural properties, particularly neurotransmitter profiles. Behavioral analyses showed that the network dynamics of bilateral motor regions were associated with the motor functions of patients with lesions. These findings offer insights into the hierarchical reorganizational principle, cortical plasticity, and neurobiological basis underlying network dynamics, and potentially guide the development of alternative treatment approaches for complex brain disorders.

items.title: Understanding the regulatory mechanisms of nanomaterials on carbon metabolism in plants
items.title_zh: Understanding the regulatory mechanisms of nanomaterials on carbon metabolism in plants
items.summary: Agricultural nanotechnology offers innovative strategies to enhance crop productivity by modulating fundamental physiological processes in plants. Despite growing evidence that nanomaterials (NMs) can significantly promote crop growth, a standardized theoretical framework explaining the underlying mechanisms remains elusive. This review proposes a systematic framework to elucidate how NMs positively regulate plant carbon assimilation and partitioning to ultimately enhance crop yield. We categorize internal carbon flow into three interconnected modules:(1) inorganic-organic carbon inter-conversion (photosynthesis and respiration), (2) organic carbon intra-conversion (sucrose and starch metabolism, alongside amino acid and fatty acid metabolism), and (3) supporting metabolic processes (nitrogen and secondary metabolism) that supply essential substrates and energy. items.summary: 中国与南非、巴西及非洲联盟联合提出“开放科学国际合作倡议”及行动计划，旨在构建开放、公平、公正、非歧视的全球科技发展环境，推动科技创新成果更多惠及“全球南方”。从愿景到落地，倡议仍需相关利益方明确推进路径并落实具体行动。不同于联合国教育、科学及文化组织（United Nations Educational，Scientific and Cultural Organization，UNESCO）发布的《开放科学建议书》定义了“开放科学是什么”，“开放科学2.0”带来更具变革性的科学场景，在基础研究领域新旧范式交替和共存的背景下，科学共同体对开放科学的期待已从研究、解决内部问题，拓展至把握人工智能机遇与应对人类共同挑战。通过案例研究、政策调研与数据分析，系统梳理了科学共同体开展开放科学国际合作的需求、挑战及开放科学2.0可能带来的解决思路，分析了开放科学价值作为国际合作共识基础、科学基金作为内部驱动力的作用机制。在结合分析了国家自然科学基金委员会资助领域的国际合作影响力与开放成熟度的基础上，建议科学基金从战略规划、制度机制和技术支撑三个层面推进开放科学国际合作：将开放科学内容纳入国际合作规划，投资开放科学国际合作能力建设，联合多方参与者尤其携手“全球南方”实现开放科学愿景，支持基础研究领域新范式实践探索，进而构建全球研究协作格局下的开放科学国际合作网络。

items.title: 植物DELLA蛋白的多重调控功能与分子机制研究进展
items.title_zh: 植物DELLA蛋白的多重调控功能与分子机制研究进展
items.summary: DELLA 基因也称为绿色革命基因(green revolution gene), 编码植物中高度保守的主要生长调控因子. 核定位的DELLA蛋白具有一个DELLA结构域和一个GRAS结构域. 它们参与GID1 (gibberellin-insensitive dwarf 1)的结合与转录激活过程, 不仅是植物中赤霉素(gibberellin, GA)信号转导途径的关键抑制因子, 而且通过与数百个转录因子和其他转录调控因子相互作用来抑制或促进基因的表达, 在转录网络枢纽以及在调控植物生长发育和响应外部环境信号中发挥着重要的作用. 本文综述了近10年来植物DELLA蛋白及其调控机制的研究进展, 主要包括DELLA蛋白在GA信号转导中的核心功能、作用机制、对植物生长发育和绿色革命的影响, 以及不依赖GA-GID1的作用, 并提出了在本领域需要进一步研究的科学问题, 试图为深入研究DELLA蛋白的分子作用机制, 以及为下一代绿色革命并提高农作物的产量与质量提供参考.

items.title: GhIAA4调控棉花抗黄萎病的分子机制研究
items.title_zh: GhIAA4调控棉花抗黄萎病的分子机制研究
items.summary: 棉花是世界上非常重要的经济作物之一, 影响棉花生长发育的真菌病害包括棉铃腐病, 黄萎病和枯萎病等多种病害. 由大丽轮枝菌引起的黄萎病是棉花生长发育及生产中面临的最重要威胁之一. 陆地棉遗传背景狭窄, 遗传多样性较低, 具有黄萎病抗性的种质十分匮乏, 挖掘棉花黄萎病抗性基因和培育棉花抗黄萎病品种是亟需解决的问题. 本研究从陆地棉( Gossypium hirsutum )中克隆生长素响应因子 GhIAA4 (Aux/IAA protein 4), 亚细胞定位结果显示GhIAA4定位在细胞核. 分析 GhIAA4 在大丽轮枝菌侵染后的表达模式, 发现该基因能够快速响应大丽轮枝菌的侵染. 利用病毒诱导的基因沉默技术下调该基因的表达, 沉默植株对黄萎病的抗性显著降低. 在拟南芥中异源过表达该基因后对黄萎病的抗性显著提升, 说明 GhIAA4 是一个正调控棉花抗病的基因. 对接种大丽轮枝菌和水对照处理后的野生型和 GhIAA4 过表达拟南芥进行转录组分析, 差异表达基因在水杨酸和茉莉酸信号途径中显著富集, 其中木葡聚糖内转糖苷酶/水解酶(xyloglucan endotransglucosylase/hydrolase, XTH )家族基因在 GhIAA4 过表达拟南芥中特异性富集, 荧光定量PCR结果表明, 该途径中的8个 XTHs 基因在 GhIAA4 过表达株系中均上调表达, 与转录组数据一致. 推测 GhIAA4 可能通过调节参与细胞壁扩张的关键基因 XTHs 的表达, 影响病原菌对棉花的入侵, 增强植株的抗病性. 综上, GhIAA4 通过参与激素和细胞壁扩张途径中的木葡聚糖转移酶来调控植物的免疫反应.

items.title: 面向科研安全的科研体系韧性与生态建设研究
items.title_zh: 面向科研安全的科研体系韧性与生态建设研究
items.summary: 在全球科技竞争日益激烈、外部遏制与封锁风险不断攀升的背景下，科研安全作为保障科研体系完整有效、核心要素供给安全可控的关键状态，正面临严峻挑战。提升科研体系韧性、构建可持续的科研体系生态，已成为筑牢国家科研安全屏障、掌握发展与竞争主动权的迫切战略需求。本文系统构建了面向科研安全的科研体系韧性与科研体系生态的理论分析框架，阐明了二者“能力—基础”的关系。通过剖析我国科研体系韧性现状，本文揭示出我国当前科研底座对外依存度高，创新生态结构尚不完善，尚未构建起结构完善、功能协同的科研体系生态，导致单点风险易汇聚成威胁科研安全的系统性风险。在此基础上，本文系统分析了美、英等国科研体系韧性提升与生态建设的政策措施，提炼了生态视角下提升科研体系韧性以保障科研安全的经验启示，进而在国家层面与国家自然科学基金委员会层面，提出聚焦提升科研韧性的“资源—主体—环境”科研体系生态建设思路。本研究旨在为推动我国科研安全实现从被动应对向主动塑造的战略转型提供理论支撑与实践参考，为建设科技强国筑牢根基。

items.title: 面向系统性风险的“生存优先”科学治理转型
items.title_zh: 面向系统性风险的“生存优先”科学治理转型
items.summary: 全球气候危机、生态失衡、能源短缺与公共卫生事件交织，人类正面临关乎文明延续的系统性生存挑战。传统以经济增长和技术竞争为核心的科学范式已难以应对跨国界、跨系统的复杂风险，全球科学治理亟需转向以“生存优先”为导向的新模式，将地球系统稳定与人类共同安全置于最高目标。这要求从成果导向走向机制导向，从竞争逻辑转向协同共治，在复杂系统科学与系统性风险分析引领下，实现学科深度融合与知识体系协作。建议通过科学外交、开放数据共享与南北合作共创等方式，重建以信任、责任与共享为基础的国际合作体系，形成面向未来的“生存安全共同体”，为全球可持续发展奠定长期支撑。以“生存优先”为核心的科学范式，正成为引领21世纪全球可持续发展与文明延续的新基石。

items.title: 重塑金融格局：数字货币时代下的脱媒效应、全球博弈与中国策略
items.title_zh: 重塑金融格局：数字货币时代下的脱媒效应、全球博弈与中国策略
items.summary: 本文系统梳理了数字货币领域的研究进展，涵盖了属性界定、金融脱媒、全球博弈、中国路径和国际协同治理五个主题。基于当前研究在理论系统性、影响机制深度和战略前瞻层面存在的明显不足，本文提出了八个亟需跨学科合作的前沿研究议题。这些议题聚焦数字货币的理论体系、中国路径的实证研究与政策制定的学理基础三大方向，旨在推动相关研究实现关键突破。本文建议应深刻认识数字货币对国家金融安全的意义，并将其发展与管理全面纳入国家金融安全的战略框架。中国应把握历史机遇，通过构建具有中国特色的数字金融治理体系与人民币国际化路径，引领创建数字货币时代的全球金融协同治理新范式，从而重塑国际货币金融秩序，为构建多元、平等、稳定的全球金融新格局贡献中国智慧。

items.title: 科技外交理论视角下国家自然科学基金深度参与全球科技治理的路径研究
items.title_zh: 科技外交理论视角下国家自然科学基金深度参与全球科技治理的路径研究
items.summary: 科技地缘政治博弈加剧使全球科技治理面临治理赤字与规则赤字的双重困境，国家自然科学基金作为我国支持基础研究国际合作的主渠道，需明确其在当前形势下参与全球科技治理的角色定位与实践路径。本文以科技外交理论为分析框架，综合运用文献研究与政策分析方法，系统考察科技外交的理论与实践演进，进而剖析国家自然科学基金在全球科技治理中的角色定位、战略价值与实践路径。本文研究提出，以资助机制创新、合作模式升级、人才体系构建、风险防控完善为核心设计国家自然科学基金深度参与全球科技治理的路径，从组织、制度、理论三个维度构建实施路径的保障机制。研究为理解科研资助机构参与全球科技治理提供了理论解释框架，对我国平衡科研开放与安全、推动构建公平包容可持续的全球科技治理体系具有参考价值。

items.title: 科学基金支持科技人才国际化发展的机制研究：基于国际比较的视角
items.title_zh: 科学基金支持科技人才国际化发展的机制研究：基于国际比较的视角
items.summary: 本文从国际嵌入程度和资助导向两个维度将世界主要国家科学基金的资助机制划分为四个象限，对美国、欧盟、德国、英国、日本等国典型科学基金进行分析，揭示科学基金支持科技人才国际化发展从个体赋能向系统共建的演化路径；将以上案例与我国现有科学基金在同一框架下展开比较分析，借鉴国际经验提出建议。研究发现，科学基金正通过纵深的资助体系与多层次合作网络，重塑科研人才国际化的结构与模式。高嵌入型机制通过跨国驻留、联合培养和制度化合作网络，显著提升了科研人员的国际协同能力与合作持续性；而低嵌入型机制则以较低成本扩大了科研人员的国际参与面，为深度合作奠定基础。借鉴有关经验，未来可从构建全周期双向培育、深化平台建设、加强开放治理三个方面完善中国科学基金的人才国际化支持体系。

items.title: 创新研究群体的科研合作特征与论文成果创新质量研究
items.title_zh: 创新研究群体的科研合作特征与论文成果创新质量研究
items.summary: 国家自然科学基金创新研究群体是我国科技创新的核心力量，厘清其科研合作特征与论文成果创新质量之间的关联机制，对于优化高水平科研团队合作策略、促进创新绩效提升具有重要意义。本研究基于国际合作、国内合作、机构内合作与产学研合作四种合作类型，引入信息熵测度该群体的科研合作多样性，并系统分析不同合作类型及合作多样性与论文成果新颖性和颠覆性之间的关系。研究结果表明：我国创新研究群体整体以国内合作为主，国际合作与机构内合作次之，产学研合作明显薄弱；合作效应方面，国际合作与论文成果新颖性、颠覆性均呈负相关，机构内合作则均呈现正相关，而国内合作与产学研合作的影响不显著；合作多样性方面，科研合作多样性与论文成果新颖性、颠覆性均呈正相关。此外，不同学科间的群体合作特征与成果创新质量关系存在显著差异。其中，数学物理科学和管理科学领域的科研合作多样性与新颖性指数正相关，与颠覆性指数负相关，说明这些领域的多样化合作更有利于促进非常规知识组合，提升成果新颖性；在化学科学、工程与材料科学、地球科学领域中，合作多样性均与新颖性指数负相关，与颠覆性指数呈现正相关关系，意味着这些领域的多样化合作更容易催生突破性成果；信息科学、医学科学、生命科学三个领域的科研合作多样性则与新颖性指数、颠覆性指数均正相关，表明这些领域的多元合作同时有助于推动知识重组与突破性创新两方面。本研究从合作类型与合作多样性双重视角揭示了创新研究群体在不同合作模式下的创新质量差异，为科研团队的合作优化与创新质量提升提供了量化依据与实践参考。

items.title_zh: 基础研究青年人才原始创新能力提升的现实挑战、影响因素及应对策略
items.summary: 基础研究青年人才是推动原始创新的重要力量，但其成长过程中面临着诸多现实挑战，亟需获得有效支持。本文基于半结构化深度访谈和大样本问卷调查，系统揭示了我国基础研究青年人才普遍面临着创新目标、科研导向、工作压力、时间管理、工作资源、评价机制等六股结构性张力，并进一步识别出六股张力现象背后，真正影响基础研究青年人才原始创新能力提升的个体特征（好奇心与内在动机、长期目标导向）、组织设计（充分稳定科研资源、大团队支持、专家点拨指导）、政策环境（宽松科研环境、延续性资助）三方面关键影响因素。最后，本文提出主动识别并培育独具好奇心和内在创新动机的青年人才，充分发挥好战略科学家、“双清论坛”等人才发展平台的引领作用、对齐国家战略需求，优化长周期支持机制和延续性资助评价体系以实现精准适配，从而真正构建起一个多层次、立体化的高质量基础研究青年人才成长生态系统。

items.title: 新形势下科学基金国际合作的思考与展望
items.title_zh: 新形势下科学基金国际合作的思考与展望
items.summary: 国家自然科学基金是支持基础研究国际合作的主渠道，是带动国际合作与交流、提高科技对外开放水平的重要工具。为设计新时期科学基金国际合作战略及实施路径主要框架，为“十五五”科学基金国际化发展战略规划提供支持，国家自然科学基金委员会举办了双清论坛“新时期科学基金国际合作战略及实施路径”。本文对论坛达成的共识进行了总结分析和进一步研究，结果表明：开展基础研究国际合作，既是科学发展的内在需要，也是科技强国建设的战略要求。与典型发达国家相类似，科学基金对国际合作的资助水平和强度不断提升，已经构建起涵盖合作研究、合作交流、外国人才等多种类别的基础研究国际合作资助体系，在扩大科技交流合作、推动知识共享、促进科研人员交流、产出重大成果等方面发挥了重要作用。然而，我国科学基金国际合作仍然面临国际形势严峻、经费资助不足、发挥作用不够、管理机制有待优化等问题和挑战。下一步，应构筑更加紧密的科研资助伙伴关系，持续完善基础研究国际合作资助体系，在平台和团队合作、国际大型联合研究、全球科技治理、引育国际人才等方面持续发力，为支撑高水平科技自立自强和科技强国建设贡献更多力量。

items.title: 创新全球科技合作机制 破解跨国合作难题
items.title_zh: 创新全球科技合作机制 破解跨国合作难题
items.summary: 创新全球科技合作机制是应对国际科技竞争格局深刻调整、促进人类可持续发展的关键举措，也是新时代科学基金推动国际合作的重要使命。本文基于国家自然科学基金委员会第419期“双清论坛”研讨成果，结合近年来国内外相关研究进展，系统梳理了全球科技合作机制的演变趋势与现实挑战，分析了跨国合作特别是南北合作中的机制障碍。研究表明，全球科技合作正呈现四大转型趋势：合作模式从松散协作向平台化机制化转型、合作逻辑从单向技术输出向共解全球性难题转变、人才流动机制从单向流动向网络化互动升级、科研经费从分散封闭向互操作化演进。针对基础研究领域合作所具有的开放性、非对称性及长周期特征，我国需加强国际合作的平台化机制建设，深化以共解全球性难题为导向的务实合作，优化国际人才流动与交流生态，创新科研经费跨境流动与管理机制，提升科学基金的引领作用，推动构建更加开放、包容、可持续的全球科技合作体系。

items.title: 系统分析框架下的国际科技合作：IIASA实践与中国系统分析能力建设路径
items.title_zh: 系统分析框架下的国际科技合作：IIASA实践与中国系统分析能力建设路径
items.summary: 在气候变化、能源危机、粮食安全等多重风险交织叠加的背景下，全球可持续发展治理正从单一目标优化转向多目标协同决策。中国“双碳”转型亟需跨尺度、跨领域的系统分析能力支撑。国际应用系统分析研究所（International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis，IIASA）在综合评估建模、科学—政策转化和多边科技合作方面积累了成熟经验。本文围绕中国转型需求、本土模型短板、IIASA优势、合作瓶颈与能力建设的逻辑主线，系统分析IIASA实践的借鉴价值，提炼其可迁移的科学—政策整合框架，提出模型本土化、跨学科研究、政策协同、人才培养等合作深化方向，为中国提升系统分析能力和参与全球可持续发展治理提供参考。

items.title: 量子计算驱动的药物研发范式演进
items.title_zh: 量子计算驱动的药物研发范式演进
items.summary: 传统模式下的药物研发面临周期长、成本高与成功率低等困境. 经典计算在处理分子电子结构、模拟微观分子互作及复杂动力学行为、解析高维生物系统难题时, 遭遇原理性瓶颈. 量子计算利用量子叠加、纠缠与干涉等独特特性, 为突破上述关键计算难题提供了全新技术路径. 本文系统综述量子计算的基本原理、全球发展态势及其在药物研发核心计算环节中的应用, 包括靶点识别、分子模拟、化合物筛选、ADMET(absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity, 即吸收、分布、代谢、排泄和毒性)性质预测及临床试验优化等; 深入剖析当前量子计算面临的主要挑战, 并展望其与人工智能深度融合、专用硬件技术突破以及产业生态协同构建等未来发展趋势. 在此基础上, 基于中药“多成分-多靶点-系统调节”复杂体系对计算能力的更高要求, 探讨了量子计算在该场景下的创新应用, 提出“分阶融合、场景驱动”的异构计算新范式, 以期为中医药现代化与精准化发展提供新思路. 总体而言, 量子计算有望突破经典计算的能力边界, 推动药物研发从传统的经验试错与局部干预模式, 向精准设计与系统调控的新范式加速演进.

items.title_zh: 新形势下国际科技合作的范式变革与应对策略
items.summary: 全球正面临逆全球化浪潮加剧与地缘政治紧张的双重挑战，科技脱钩风险显著上升，应对气候变化、公共卫生、数据治理等重大全球性挑战领域的国际科技合作受到严重阻碍。本文全面审视当前国际科技合作面临的新形势与新问题，明确国际科技合作的战略价值与范式变革需求，探讨我国开展国际科技合作的方向性布局与研究支撑。研究提出了应强化科技合作的显性效能、创新科技伦理与治理议程、推动科技共享与成果普惠、深化科技外交与人文交流等建议，推动构建更加开放、包容和创新的国际科技合作机制和方法。

items.title: “硬核科技外交”赋能全球科技治理——人类可持续发展的科技合作新范式
items.title_zh: “硬核科技外交”赋能全球科技治理——人类可持续发展的科技合作新范式
items.summary: 本文基于第419期“双清论坛”研讨成果，提出并阐释“硬核科技外交”概念。采用文献分析、案例归纳与体系建构方法，梳理全球科技格局与中国科技外交发展及制度瓶颈，构建“科技—机制—人才—治理”四元联动体系模型。研究表明，“硬核科技外交”以重大科技基础设施、关键核心技术等为支撑，是我国参与全球科技治理、提升制度性话语权的重要途径。通过多领域实践案例分析，总结出“五维协同”特征，证实其是中国从全球治理“参与者”向“引领者”转变的制度创新路径。未来需通过完善顶层设计、强化科技安全与开放平衡等措施，构建科技合作新范式，为全球科技治理贡献中国智慧与方案。

items.title: 进入行星大气极端流动与传热基础科学问题
items.title_zh: 进入行星大气极端流动与传热基础科学问题
items.summary: 深空探测正向更远天体、更高速度、更大载荷发展，面临极端流动与传热的严峻挑战。高速进入行星大气的探测器面临可达数万开尔文的流场环境，超高温物理化学反应与宏观流动、流固界面传热传质等多个过程紧密耦合，对探测器安全构成重大威胁。深刻认知其中的关键物理机理，是突破气动与防热设计瓶颈、实现高可靠轻量化任务的基础科学前提。本文系统阐述了该领域亟待突破的三个核心科学问题：极高速复杂流动多过程耦合作用机理、强辐射传热环境下材料响应与防热机理、行星大气超高温多相态非平衡理化反应机理。基于国内外研究规划与进展，分析了当前主要挑战——现有模型多基于较低温（≤8 000 K）空气介质数据，外推至高焓环境风险大；态—态方法精度高但基础数据匮乏；地面实验难以复现真实飞行环境，相似理论与多尺度模拟方法尚不完善等。针对上述瓶颈，探讨了创新研究思路：发展微观反应降阶建模与流动微介观描述方法相结合的“升—降尺度”紧耦合数值框架；探索辐射屏蔽、梯度防热等多机制协同策略，建立强辐射环境下材料响应与热量调控新理论；构建基于第一性原理计算与先进原子分子实验的高精度反应数据库等。通过持续研究有望建立能够精确表征多相态、多尺度、多过程、强耦合的极端流动与传热新理论，并从地球大气向多行星大气拓展，为下一代深空探测器系统设计提供科学基础与技术支撑。

items.title: 科技竞争下受资助人任职海外的数据安全风险与对策
items.title_zh: 科技竞争下受资助人任职海外的数据安全风险与对策
items.summary: 随着全球科技竞争加剧，各国密集出台人才招募政策，导致科研人员任职海外日趋频繁，易引发数据安全风险。特别是随着受资助人范围逐步扩大及跨国流动性增强，我国科研资助机构面临的数据安全风险进一步加剧，主要表现为受资助人任职海外后中断数据汇交、泄露敏感数据、目的导向研究造成数据失真等。问题原因在于我国资助机构的数据汇交、强制性披露、数据质量监测及问责等机制存在不足。为此，我国可借鉴外国经验，将受资助人列为数据汇交首要责任人，搭建加密海外汇交通道；健全任职海外全周期披露制度，明确披露要素及时限；依据“可发现（findable）、可访问（accessible）‌、可互操作（interoperable）‌、可重用（reusable）”原则（以下简称“FAIR原则”）完善数据质量监测；建立多元惩戒与跨国协同问责机制，推动受资助人、依托单位切实履责，筑牢科研数据安全防线。

items.title_zh: 五轮驱动：构建教育、科技与人才一体化的国际合作新模式
items.summary: 全球可持续发展目标（Sustainable Development Goals，SDGs）推进总体滞后，国际合作体系在资源配置、协同机制与包容性方面面临深层挑战。本文分析了国际科研资助机构合作模式的最新趋势，指出我国在国际合作中存在战略协同不足、资源分布过度集中、学科壁垒突出、评价体系短期化及地缘政治制约等突出问题。因此，提出以“全球引智、平台共建、协同创新、人才联培、人文交流”为核心的“五轮驱动”国际合作新模式。该模式形成了涵盖人才汇聚、科技攻坚、教育赋能、信任筑基与文化互鉴的系统框架，通过国际专家工作站、联合科研平台及双导师制等手段，实现教育、科技与人才一体化联动。我们认为，“五轮驱动”模式可形成自我增强的协同体系，有效提升我国参与全球可持续发展治理的能力与贡献，为“十五五”时期构建开放包容、高效协同的国际合作体系提供理论支撑与实践路径。

items.title_zh: 一氧化氮供体的设计合成及用于糖尿病伤口治疗的研究
items.summary: 一氧化氮(NO)是一种重要的生物信号分子, 在抗菌、生物膜抑制、炎症调控以及血管生成等过程中发挥重要作用, 因而在糖尿病伤口治疗中具有广阔的应用前景. 本文综述了NO供体的设计合成及其在糖尿病伤口治疗中的研究进展. 根据来源和结构特性将NO供体分为内源性与外源性两大类, 总结了其设计与合成的基本原理和方法, 介绍了几种典型的NO供体的特性和治疗策略, 阐述了NO供体在糖尿病伤口中的治疗机制并分析了供体的物理和化学特性对治疗效果及安全性的影响. 然而在糖尿病伤口独特的微环境中, 内源性NO的合成受到限制, 外源性NO供体释放精度较差. 基于此, 本文进一步分析讨论了NO供体在糖尿病伤口治疗应用中面临的挑战, 并提出未来研究应重点关注智能响应型NO供体的设计以及协同治疗平台的开发.

items.title: 面向自适应通信增强的可移动智能超表面
items.title_zh: 面向自适应通信增强的可移动智能超表面
items.summary: 随着5G/6G、毫米波通信和车联网等应用场景对可靠覆盖和高数据速率的需求持续攀升, 复杂环境中的信道衰落与遮挡问题逐渐成为影响通信性能的核心瓶颈. 智能超表面(reconfigurable intelligent surface, RIS)因其低功耗、可编程和易部署等优势, 成为提升无线通信质量的重要技术. 然而, 传统固定式RIS受限于空间刚性与场景变化, 难以在动态环境中保持稳定增益. 为此, 本文提出一种集视觉感知、三维建图、路径规划与电磁调控于一体的可移动智能超表面系统, 构建了“视觉感知—场景重建—位置/码本联合优化—通信增强”的闭环体系. 系统采用ZED 2i立体视觉实现对环境的三维点云重建, 并生成栅格地图用于障碍识别与路径规划; 基于双层粒子群优化算法同时优化RIS部署位置与编码模式, 使可移动平台能自主移动至最优反射点位并实现波束聚焦. 实验结果表明, 系统在不同光照条件下均能获得结构完整、密度均匀的三维重建结果, 平均定位误差小于 0.05 m, 角度误差小于3°, 满足实时路径规划需求. 在通信性能方面, 相比“无RIS”场景, 可移动RIS显著提升接收信号强度, 丢包率降低68.3%; 与固定RIS相比, 移动式部署进一步改善链路稳定性与星座图稳定性, 使通信信号解调更为准确. 本研究验证了可移动智能超表面在弱覆盖区域链路构建与动态复杂场景通信质量增强中的有效性, 为构建自适应、环境智能化的6G通信系统提供了一种可行的技术路径.

items.title: 基于克里金代理模型的雷达/红外兼容隐身结构优化
items.title_zh: 基于克里金代理模型的雷达/红外兼容隐身结构优化
items.summary: 针对现代多频谱兼容隐身技术中多设计参数与多性能目标带来的复杂电磁优化挑战, 本文基于在线模型的机器学习辅助优化方法来实现超表面隐身结构的高效设计. 首先, 通过引入可靠的可变保真度模型进行初始采样, 有效降低全波仿真带来的计算成本. 在代理模型训练过程中, 自适应地选择训练策略来更新模型, 缓解因设计维数增加而引起的训练时间增长问题. 此外, 结合全局多目标优化的混合策略, 进一步提升算法在复杂解空间中的收敛性能. 基于上述方法, 我们成功设计并制备出一种雷达/红外兼容隐身的复合超表面. 该结构采用红外低发射层与雷达吸波层一体化架构, 通过在功能层表面印刷高阻碳浆图案并优化其尺寸, 在2.8~20 GHz频带内实现了高于90%的宽带高效吸收. 同时, 通过提高表面金属贴片占空比, 将结构在红外波段的发射率控制在约0.25的低水平. 实验结果表明, 所设计结构兼具优异的宽频雷达吸波性能与低红外发射率特征. 本研究验证了所提优化方法在雷达/红外兼容隐身设计中的高效性, 大幅缩短了优化训练时间, 为多频谱兼容隐身材料的设计提供了有效解决方案.

items.title: 非线性层关键参数与衍射神经网络性能的关联研究
items.title_zh: 非线性层关键参数与衍射神经网络性能的关联研究
items.summary: 随着人工智能技术的飞速发展, 电子计算在功耗与算力层面正日益逼近物理极限. 衍射神经网络凭借其低功耗、光速运算与高度并行处理能力, 成为突破现有电子计算瓶颈的重要技术路径之一. 非线性作为提升衍射神经网络性能的核心已引起学界的广泛关注, 但现有研究多集中于非线性层的硬件实现, 对网络架构中非线性机制的系统性分析较为缺乏. 尤其关键的是, 非线性层的位置、数量以及激活函数类型等结构参数尚未得到充分探索, 因此在相当程度上制约了高性能非线性衍射神经网络的进一步发展与优化. 为此, 本文以人体动作识别为典型任务, 系统探究了非线性层数量、位置及激活函数类型对识别性能的影响规律. 实验结果表明, 上述结构参数对系统识别准确率具有显著影响. 因此, 在实际应用中需结合具体任务需求进行全面评估, 以确定最佳网络参数配置, 从而充分释放非线性衍射神经网络的性能潜力. 本研究系统揭示了网络结构参数与识别准确率之间的内在联系, 为高性能非线性衍射神经网络的结构设计与优化提供了理论依据与方法支撑.

items.title: 基于多模态感知的双频共口径智能超表面通信系统
items.title_zh: 基于多模态感知的双频共口径智能超表面通信系统
items.summary: 为满足6G对超高数据速率与极低时延的迫切需求, 毫米波通信成为关键支撑技术, 但其易受阻塞、波束管理困难等挑战制约了在动态场景中的应用. 可重构智能超表面(reconfigurable intelligent metasurfaces, RIS)可动态调控无线信道以克服毫米波通信的遮挡和衰减, 然而, 现有超表面系统严重依赖高开销、高复杂度的信道状态信息(channel state information, CSI)估计. 为此, 本文提出一种基于人工智能(artificial intelligent, AI)的“智能感知-无线通信一体化”创新架构, 通过对AI模型进行训练和验证, 实现对智能终端的快速识别, 促进从“反应式”到“感知驱动式”通信的范式转变. 本研究核心包括: (1) 设计了一款X波段与Ka波段的双频共口径智能超表面, 并通过子阵拼接的方式, 构建超大规模阵列以实现双频的精准波束调控; (2) 提出一种视觉与电磁信息融合的多模态定位方法, 通过前期数据集的训练使其能够对无人机进行感知, 融合YOLOv8的目标识别优势与射频信号的精确测距能力, 克服单一传感器的局限性; (3) 基于AI感知直接驱动超表面波束赋形, 规避传统CSI估计的瓶颈. 通过面向无人机毫米波通信场景的实验验证表明, 该架构能实现对终端的精确定位、毫米波通信信号增强等, 为未来低空经济中的毫米波可靠通信和无线传能提供了有效的技术路径.

items.title: 智能超材料与超材料智能的前沿进展
items.title_zh: 智能超材料与超材料智能的前沿进展
items.summary: 超材料与人工智能的相互作用正形成两个双向耦合的新兴方向: 智能超材料与超材料智能. 智能超材料是指通过智能算法实现按需设计和自适应电磁调控, 推动其在隐身、通信与成像等场景中应用; 超材料智能, 又称类脑超材料, 是以电磁波作为计算载体, 通过利用可调谐结构、非线性效应与多维度复用在电磁空间直接计算, 构造神经网络和数学算符的同素异形体, 实现光速推理、分析与信息处理. 这两个方向共同推动超材料从单一功能器件向具备感知、决策与执行能力的超材料智能体演进. 本文以“物理机制—算法协同—系统应用”架构为主线, 系统梳理两大方向的核心原理、方法体系与前沿进展, 重点分析两者在智能实现方式与系统目标上的差异, 进一步探讨在物理-数据一致性、器件可重构性与系统集成等方面的挑战, 并展望物理驱动的少样本与在线学习方法, 推动超材料走向可部署的智能工程化系统.

items.title: 电磁超材料与人工智能: 从智能赋能到自主智能
items.title_zh: 电磁超材料与人工智能: 从智能赋能到自主智能
items.summary: 超材料与人工智能(AI)的交互方式, 已历经“结构‑响应”精准映射辅助设计、“波基计算”硬件创新、有源器件实时调控电磁波, 再到超材料智能体与智能体超材料的智能自主协同. 本文系统综述二者融合的基础架构、前沿进展与未来展望. 基础架构方面, 正向设计依托梯度优化、启发式算法与深度学习代理模型实现高效映射; 逆向设计借助判别式与生成式模型应对“多对多映射”难题, 物理知情、数据增强与迁移学习技术显著提升模型泛化能力. 前沿突破涵盖机械可编程超材料与光学计算实现的低功耗波基计算、依托有源器件智能实时调控电磁波实现动态适应、基于大语言模型实现智能体超材料的“感知‑推理‑执行”认知能力, 以及超材料智能体构建超材料无人监督设计流程. 未来需从智能体推理鲁棒性、跨场景迁移性与硬件微型化集成三个维度突破. 本文通过梳理“基础架构—前沿突破—未来展望”的技术脉络, 为超材料与人工智能从“智能赋能”向“自主智能”演进提供参考.

items.title: 深度遗传算法驱动的超宽带透明隐身超表面设计
items.title_zh: 深度遗传算法驱动的超宽带透明隐身超表面设计
items.summary: 电磁隐身技术是信息功能材料领域的关键方向之一, 对提升复杂环境下的电磁兼容性与信息防护能力具有重要意义. 面向宽频段电磁散射抑制、器件薄型化、光学透明以及宽入射角稳健性等多重需求, 传统吸波材料一方面受限于材料本征的光学不透明性, 另一方面受Rozanov厚度–带宽极限约束, 难以同时满足现代透明电子设备对可见光通透性与微波隐身性的双重要求. 为此, 本文提出了一种深度学习与遗传算法融合的智能设计方法——深度遗传算法(deep genetic algorithm, DGA), 并基于该算法设计了一种基于氧化铟锡(indium tin oxide, ITO)的超宽带透明吸波隐身超表面. 在 DGA中, 前向预测网络以数据驱动方式作为全波电磁仿真的替代评估模型, 从而显著提升结构评估与优化迭代效率; 遗传算法在高维参数空间内进行约束优化, 在满足总厚度限制的同时提升器件在不同入射角下的带宽稳定性. 实验结果表明, 所制备样品实现了覆盖S波段高频段至Ka波段 (3.5~35 GHz )的超宽带吸收, 相对带宽高达163%, 同时保持60%以上的光学透光率, 且在0°~50°的入射角范围内保持了稳定的全极化宽带隐身响应. 本研究为“光学透明－电磁隐身”功能一体化表面的实现提供了全新技术路径与器件原型, 在透明电子、车载隐身窗口及建筑电磁兼容等领域具有应用潜力.
